name: Earth & Solar System
description: The Solar System defines the observer-centered origin of this atlas. Catalog directions and radial distances are transformed into display coordinates from this reference point.

name: Proxima Centauri
type: High proper-motion M-dwarf / Alpha Centauri component
distance_basis: Direct inverse-parallax visualization distance; formal measurement uncertainty only.
description: The nearest known star to the Sun. Position, proper motion and parallax in this build are transcribed from the SIMBAD record, whose astrometry cites Gaia EDR3.

name: Sirius A / B
type: Spectroscopic binary; A-type primary + white dwarf
description: The brightest star system in Earth’s night sky. The position, proper motion, parallax and radial velocity shown here are catalog measurements surfaced through SIMBAD.

name: Vega (Alpha Lyrae)
description: A bright A-type standard star. SIMBAD lists the ICRS position, proper motion, parallax and radial velocity used in this embedded record.

name: Arcturus (Alpha Boötis)
description: A nearby orange giant with high proper motion. Astrometry and radial velocity are embedded from the SIMBAD record and its cited literature.

name: Pleiades Cluster (M45)
distance_basis: Inverse of the catalog mean parallax for atlas visualization; cluster depth is not represented.
description: The Pleiades open cluster. The embedded SIMBAD record reports a mean parallax of 7.364 mas and proper motion values from Gaia-era cluster astrometry.

name: Betelgeuse (Alpha Orionis)
distance_basis: Naive inverse-parallax display distance; uncertainty/systematics are scientifically significant.
description: A nearby red supergiant whose distance is difficult to estimate precisely. v3 intentionally exposes the large uncertainty rather than presenting a false single-value precision.

name: Orion Nebula (M42)
distance_basis: Literature trigonometric-parallax distance to the Orion Nebula Cluster.
description: The Orion Nebula / Orion Nebula Cluster region. The sky position is from SIMBAD; the adopted distance is a published VLBA trigonometric-parallax result.

name: Sagittarius A* (Galactic Centre)
distance_basis: Geometric Galactic-centre distance from the S2 orbit.
description: The compact radio source associated with the Milky Way’s central black hole. Position is from SIMBAD; distance uses the GRAVITY Collaboration geometric S2-orbit measurement.

name: Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC)
distance_basis: Eclipsing-binary geometric distance; preferred over using local peculiar redshift.
description: A major Milky Way satellite and a cornerstone of the extragalactic distance ladder. Position and redshift are from SIMBAD; distance uses late-type eclipsing binaries.

name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
distance_basis: Adopted heliocentric Local Group distance 783 ± 25 kpc; redshift is not used as a Hubble-flow distance.
description: The dominant large galaxy of the Local Group alongside the Milky Way. The ICRS position and heliocentric redshift are from SIMBAD; a literature distance is adopted because peculiar velocity dominates locally.

name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
distance_basis: Adopted TRGB distance 809 ± 24 kpc; local peculiar velocity makes redshift unsuitable as a distance proxy.
description: The third-largest major galaxy of the Local Group. ICRS position and observed redshift come from SIMBAD; distance is a TRGB-based literature value.

name: Centaurus A (NGC 5128)
description: The nearest powerful radio galaxy. SIMBAD supplies the precise radio position and observed redshift; the adopted distance comes from a multi-method distance review.

name: 3C 273
distance_basis: Comoving distance numerically derived from observed z using this build’s Planck-2018-like cosmology.
description: The historically first identified quasar. Its precise ICRS direction and spectroscopic redshift are embedded from SIMBAD; radial distance is derived from that observed redshift under the atlas ΛCDM model.

name: Virgo Cluster (context centre)
description: Representative center used to navigate the Virgo-region scale. This is a contextual atlas landmark, not a precision centroid or a substitute for member-galaxy catalog data.

name: Great Attractor region
source_ref: Extended region; no single-point catalog identity
description: A navigation marker for the Great Attractor / Norma region. The phenomenon is extended and model-dependent; the point shown here is deliberately labeled as context rather than an observed object.

name: Coma Cluster (context)
description: Representative Coma Cluster landmark retained for scale navigation. The point is contextual; individual member galaxies should be used for precision catalog work.

name: Shapley Supercluster region
description: Representative marker for the Shapley concentration. It is an extended structure and is therefore not represented as a precision point measurement.

name: Boötes Void region
description: A representative point for navigating the Boötes Void scale. The void is spatially extended; this marker is not a physical object at a single coordinate.

name: Sloan Great Wall region
description: A representative navigation point for the Sloan Great Wall scale. The wall is an extended galaxy distribution, not a point source.

name: Cosmic Microwave Background
distance_basis: Numerical comoving distance under the atlas cosmological model.
description: The last-scattering surface rendered at the model comoving distance corresponding to z ≈ 1089. The sphere texture is procedural and must not be interpreted as Planck sky-map data.
